---
type: mobilization
id: mob-gluteus-medius-ball
title: Gluteus medius ball release
targets: [FMA:22315, FMA:22317]
joint: FMA:24964
kind: self_myofascial
steps:
  - Stand with your side to a wall and place a firm ball between the wall and the area just below the iliac crest.
  - Shift weight onto the ball and roll slowly over the posterolateral hip until a tender spot is found.
  - Hold gentle pressure on the spot while breathing out; pressure should feel like a "good ache", not sharp pain.
  - After 30 to 60 seconds, move to the next tender spot.
duration: 1 to 2 minutes per side
frequency: Once daily, or before hip-abductor exercises
contraindications:
  - Recent hip surgery or fracture
  - Acute inflammation, skin lesions, or bruising over the area
  - Anticoagulant therapy without medical clearance
sources: [travell-simons-vol2]
---
Ischaemic compression with a ball against a wall is a practical way to reach the
posterior fibres of gluteus medius, which are hard to stretch effectively. Follow up
with side-lying hip abduction to restore strength in the released muscle.
